newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's co-ruling Peasants to oust farm minister.
newsitem.headline: Poland's co-ruling Peasants to oust farm minister.

text.p: The Polish Peasant Party (PSL), the smaller partner in the ruling coalition, said it decided on Wednesday that its agriculture minister Roman Jagielinski should be sacked for failing to safeguard farmers' interests.

The party's executive committee said in a statement that it wanted Jagielinski, who is also deputy prime minister, to be replaced in both functions by his fellow Peasant Party parliamentary deputy, Jaroslaw Kalinowski, 35.

"The Supreme Executive Council of the PSL, taking into account the situation in agriculture and the food economy, withdraws our colleague Roman Jagielinski from the functions of deputy prime minister and agriculture minister," said the statement read out to a news conference.

The statement, read by PSL spokesman Aleksander Bentkowski, said the party had sacked Jagielinski because of wrong decisions which led to a Polish food and commodities trade deficit of $1 billion last year, and over inadequate interventions on the market causing livestock prices to fall.
It said there had been a drop in grain and pig purchases.

The party accused Jagielinski of inadequate supervision of the State Agency for Agricultural Property, managing land which formerly belonged to huge state-owned farms, saying this had prevented farmers from buying land to increase the size of their holdings.
Bentkowski said the PSL did not expect ex-communist Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, who ultimately appoints and dismisses cabinet ministers, to oppose the PSL's decision.

Last week Cimoszewicz replaced Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko with Marek Belka, without consulting the Peasants, arguing that the finance portfolio was at the disposal of his own Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) under the two parties' coalition agreement.
"Since there were no discussions on the appointment of Mr Belka, there won't be any discussions now," Bentkowski said, underlining that the farm ministry belonged to the PSL.

Jagielinski, a large landowner, has been seen by many of his colleagues as having more sympathy for the market reform priorities of the ex-communists -- over issues including the need for fast entry into the European Union -- than with the needs of the many small farmers who make up the PSL ranks.
Last year Jagielinski unsuccessfully challenged the Party president Waldemar Pawlak in a bitter leadership contest.
In a meeting on Saturday, the party's national council strongly criticised government agriculture policy, but stopped short of dropping Jagielinski.
